what_they_do: UserJourneys is an experimentation and analytics tool for product engineers at consumer software companies. It connects to a company's existing analytics and warehouse tools (BigQuery, Snowflake, PostHog, Mixpanel, Amplitude), automatically builds a graph of user events showing where people drop off or convert, and triggers AI-run interviews with the specific users who hit a friction point, launched by email, push notification, or in-app prompt. It replaces the manual process of a product team digging through session replays by hand, guessing which users to interview about a given drop-off, and stitching together custom dashboards to track a journey across tools.
vertical: Product analytics / experimentation software for consumer tech companies
theme_fit_rationale: UserJourneys reads unstructured and structured signals across analytics warehouses, product event streams, and communication channels (email, push, in-app), then writes back a targeted user interview and feeds the result into the product graph, a cross-system feedback loop that fits Theme 2's pattern of agents consolidating fragmented tools and using proximity to the user to build a proprietary, compounding dataset.
workflow_artifacts: analytics and data warehouse integrations (BigQuery, Snowflake, PostHog, Mixpanel, Amplitude)
prior_insights: Lauri, I was looking at how you guys trigger the AI interviews based on behavioral signals rather than random sampling. I think that's the right approach because the most useful feedback comes from users at the exact moment something breaks, not from a survey link they get two weeks later. Curious how many interviews it typically takes before the product graph starts surfacing actionable patterns.

Lauri, the Jungler case study caught my attention. Doubling their conversion rate by catching bugs that were silently killing conversions is a concrete result. Most tools would have shown the drop-off but not told them why.

I'd be curious whether you're seeing more pull from PLG companies optimizing onboarding or from teams trying to reduce churn.

Lauri, last thought from me. We've worked closely with companies in the PLG space like Calendly and Expensify, and the analytics-to-action gap you're solving is something that comes up constantly. If it would be useful, happy to connect you with a couple of product leaders in our network who are actively trying to solve this problem.

If now isn't the right time, totally understand.
